doc.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08

chapter: Eureka Brass Band and Sonny Henry
title: Sonny Henry on Jim, tailgate trombone who cannot read
summary: Sonny Henry describes Jim as a strong tailgate man who never learned to read and only plays comfortably with his friends.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: But I'm going to tell you about Jim, about Jim. I just wish that, that, that, that I could play with him in a way of speaking, understand? Of course I, I know that I'm a, his superior, you understand? But, in, uh, his style of playing, understand? And Jim, if you ever get in there one time, boy, he, got to make you sick. Mm-hmm. But he, he, he, that man don't forget nothing though. No, he got a lot of life to it. I'm going to tell you, you, you, you can say what you want. Take care of nobody, see, Jim is a good, tailgate man. Mm-hmm. That's right. Me, I've tried my whole life, to, to, to try and make him, learn how to read like I could. But if Jim had learned the way I learned. Jim never even want to learn how to read. If Jim had learned the way I learned, Jim would be one, one, one of the best trombone players in the city.

I wonder, did Jim learn to read a little bit? He told me once he could read some, but I thought maybe his eyes, you know, his eyes aren't too good for reading without glasses. I thought maybe that was part of it.
He still couldn't read even the glasses. This, this, this man thought his damnness to buy him out of reading.

That's, that's the same. I wondered whether he really wanted to or not. No, no, no, this is the truth. I'm telling you a lot. Yeah. His head ain't right. But, I'm going to tell you, that's some good even players. I'll, I'll tell you the world, anytime you jump on Jim, you're going to jump on a man. With, with, with his band and you put in the team there. But now, of course, if he, if he's going to, going to come out with, with, with the Eureka. No. It's a different attitude. You got to, change, change, change your level. If you do, you're in a hell of a face.

Just like he said, he says, if Sonny is there or I'm there, he don't mind filling in for either one of us. Yeah, I've heard him get along pretty well. But if, he said, if either one of us ain't there, he said, he don't want to play.

No. Because it's inside him. You see, I don't want against him. Against him. Nobody. If I get back up. You understand? That's the. But now, if a guy want to come in and see what he can do. This thing, you know. Well, I'm going to try and do it. You see, when he, A party get in the party now. I'm going to take my whole line. I'm going to see what he's going to do. But if a person comes out. You understand? Be nice. But I'm sure. Again. My band. I'm going to let my band fall. For. Trying to take a. Revenge. Or. Come on in there. In our band, that's what we do.
